Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Time, the calendar & feasts

former adjective

earlier, once but no longer

also ex-, one-time, formerly, as it used to be

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.5b.2: tua prīstina dignitās et glōria (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 7.54: in prīstinum statum redīssent

1prīstinus: long first i (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 489, s.v. prior: from the zero grade *prīs- of the comparative, as in prīscus and prīdem.

prīstinus1, prīstina, prīstinum

adjective, declension

former, earlier, as it once was

Of a state, a habit or a standing one had before: in prīstinum statum redīre, to go back to how things were.

Other words

  • quondam — once, formerly (with a noun: former)

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 154: quī quondam in hostīs lēnissimus exīstimābātur, hōc tempore; Tib. 3.1.23: vir quondam, nunc frāter (Lewis & Short)

    Latin has no adjective for a former husband or a former teacher; it says what he once was: vir quondam, “once a husband”, or with a clause, quī … fuit.

  • superior, superius — earlier, former (of time)

    adjective (comparative), declension · also used · classical · Cic. Har. Resp. 15: annō superiōre (Lewis & Short)

    Of time before the present Cicero says superior (Lewis & Short, s.v. prior); see last (the one before this).

  • anteā — formerly, before

    also used · classical · Traupman 318

Examples

  • hoc sī quis pretiī cupidus vīdisset tuī, ōlim redīssēs ad splendōrem prīstinum

    if someone who knew your worth had seen you, you would long ago have gone back to your former splendourPhaedr. 3.12.4–5

  • patre itaque meō rogante … ad prīstinam cōnsuētūdinem rediī

    so, at my father’s request, … I went back to my former habitSen. Ep. 108.22

  • populum Rōmānum, quī quondam in hostīs lēnissimus exīstimābātur, hōc tempore domesticā crūdēlitāte labōrāre

    that the Roman people, once thought the gentlest of nations even towards its enemies, now suffers from cruelty at homeCic. Rosc. Am. 154

See also last, former, original, normal.
